pages.title: Get started
pages.description: Find your workspace, sign in and identify your next task.

Choose your workspace: Open the service appropriate to your assignment. Staff use the Staff Portal or a direct service link. Applicants use Household Registration or the Beneficiary Portal.
The Master Registry holds intake, duplicate review and approved records. Data Imports is a workspace within it. PBMS manages programmes, list approval and payment progress.
Sign in: Use the email assigned to the relevant service. Staff services may redirect to the shared identity provider. PBMS has its own sign-in screen and programme assignments.
After sign-in, check the workspace name and the assigned role. If an expected queue is missing, check with your service administrator using the service name and your account email.
Use the sandbox: Use synthetic people, identifiers, accounts and payments. Guides describe the installed sandbox. Agency policies, thresholds and formal operating procedures require approval.

pages.title: Service directory
pages.description: Find the installed services and the guides that explain how to use them.

pages.title: Service delivery lifecycle
pages.description: Follow a case from capture to publication, benefit approval and reconciliation.

Register and review: Capture a household or individual in the Master Registry, or bring submissions through the supported import path. Save and submit the record. A field submission enters Level 1 review and may advance to Level 2 for publication.
Assess and approve: PBMS uses the target registry and the programme’s eligibility configuration to calculate enrolment and disbursement lists. Staff complete the configured approval chain before Payment can submit a verified revision.
Dispatch and reconcile: Bridge processes the authorised instructions. Financial addresses are resolved through the configured mapper, then the sponsor bank route is used. Finance checks the statement evidence and follows up on unresolved or reversed instructions.
Follow a case across services: Use the reference issued by each workspace. An intake reference, beneficiary application ID, PBMS list revision, batch and envelope identify different records or stages.

pages.title: Household registration
pages.description: Register a household, submit it for staff review and correct returned details.

Choose the household workspace: This Household Registration workspace uses a Registration Officer and a Verification Officer. The native Master Beneficiary Registry uses Form submissions and assigned Level 1 and Level 2 review tasks. Use the guide for the workspace displayed after sign-in.
Prepare the profile: Record the applicant as the head and add the members of the same household. Use the displayed formats for names, birth dates and location. Enter submitted or device coordinates only when they describe the household.
Submit and follow up: Check the roster and synthetic declaration before sending for review. Open the workspace to see the case status. If the record comes back, read the reason, correct the existing profile and send it again.
After approval: Check the registry connection status. Once connected, follow the relevant programme’s application process.

pages.title: Registration review workspace
pages.description: Verify household details and record an independent decision.

Identify your review workspace: Use this guide for Household Registration’s Verification Officer workspace. In the native Master Beneficiary Registry, follow the separately assigned Level 1 or Level 2 task.
Open the next case: Select the Verification officer workspace and open an awaiting case. Read the earlier reason and review history when a correction has been requested.
Complete the checks: Review the household and member roster. Decide whether the current evidence is complete, whether the previous reason has been addressed, and whether you are ready to approve the registration itself.
Approve or return: For a correctable issue, explain exactly what needs changing. Approval connects the registration to the registries. Track connection status from the case.

pages.title: Master Beneficiary Registry
pages.description: Capture and find household and individual records, review submissions and maintain approved records.

Find a record: Open Households or Individuals to browse approved master records. Open Form submissions for drafts, pending submissions or revalidation. Reviewers open their assigned tasks from My tasks.
Capture and submit: Create the appropriate intake. For household intake, complete the consent and enumeration section, verify the geographic hierarchy, add the head and household members, and work through the dwelling, income, health, assets and crop sections. Save edited sections and confirm the household information before submitting.
Work with master records: Open an approved record to inspect its details and version history. If your assigned role shows a change-request action, use the separate change-request workflow and retain the target record reference. Read-only access supports inspection.
Registry administration: Administrators manage authorised staff configuration and approved register metadata. Use the corresponding view for inbound and outbound messages when following an integration issue.
Choose a dashboard entry point: Use Register your household if your assigned role displays it. Reviewers open their assigned tasks in My tasks. The Registry Officer inspects approved records from Households or Individuals.

pages.title: Registry review and duplicate checks
pages.description: Compare match evidence, return a draft for correction or advance an assigned submission.

Review at the right level: Level 1 checks the assigned submission and advances it to Level 2 when approved. Level 2 reviews the current submission and the Level 1 decision. Final approval publishes the approved record for the Registry Officer.
Compare duplicate candidates: Intake Duplicates compares other intake submissions. Existing Duplicates compares published Registry records visible to your role. Each candidate appears once per tab. Open View More to read the strongest comparison and its incoming values, candidate values and field-level similarity.
If a tab has no visible result and you have other evidence of a possible match, use the approved escalation route and provide the submission reference to an authorised Registry Administrator.
Revalidate or reject: Use Revalidate when the original field agent can correct the submission. Write the reason and the section to revisit. The creator opens it under Revalidation, corrects the same draft and submits it again. Both return paths restart at Level 1.
The screenshot labels this return action Return for correction. In the tested native workflow, use Revalidate to send the existing draft back and Revalidation to find it as the creator.
Apply the authorised review rules before permanent rejection. Keep identifiers and personal details in their dedicated fields and approved evidence channels.
How task levels and role labels relate: Level 1 and Level 2 identify task stages in Form submissions and Approvals. In this sandbox, the Help panel identifies the assigned roles as First Reviewer and Second Reviewer. Check the assigned role and the stage before acting.

For a return, the creator corrects the original submission and resubmits it. The same submission goes back to Level 1 before it can reach Level 2. The published Registry record becomes available after final approval.

pages.title: Data Imports and Data Bridge
pages.description: Prepare and approve a batch, then follow its native Registry transfer and receipt.

Start with the batch workflow: For a standard import, prepare the batch, review and transfer it, then check the Registry receipt. Expand the section matching your exception for parallel imports, partial receipts and recovery.
Prepare the batch: Select the configured data source and check Expected columns. Upload CSV or XLSX, or fetch CSV from a configured connection. The workspace supports up to 2 MB, 1,000 data rows and 40 columns. XLSX uses the first worksheet.
Check source and mapped Registry values. Resolve required fields and duplicate keys within the batch. Save each correction or exclusion and confirm which rows will transfer.
Fetch a connected CSV: In New import, choose a connected source, check Expected columns and select Fetch and validate. A new fetch opens a draft. Use Reconcile records to review the mapped rows before sending the draft for approval.

For a sandbox test, choose Synthetic connected CSV test only. Its CSV contains Reference and Test note columns and a duplicate reference. Resolve or exclude the duplicate and save the row before requesting approval.

If the browser loses the response, sign in with the same Registry login, choose the same source and use Fetch and validate. If the batch was saved, it opens at its current status even when both browsers retry together. Use Fetch a new CSV on the recovered batch only when you intend to start a separate import. Transfers and Refresh history can also locate the attempted batch by source and time.

Ask the integration administrator to verify the server-side HTTPS configuration and CSV response if the error persists. To check a batch already sent to the Registry, refresh its existing receipt in Transfers.
Choose between separate connected import: When one browser starts a separate CSV import and another retries the original, each action keeps its own batch. If two browsers use Fetch a new CSV from the same earlier batch, both open the same separate draft. If they start from different originals, each original gets its own follow-up, even when both use the same source.

If a browser asks you to choose a match, open Transfers and select Refresh history. Use Batch reference to open the intended import and Previous batch reference to confirm which original it follows. A source, filename and time may appear on multiple batches.
Verify parallel CSV imports by role: As Field Agent, open two different original batches for the same connected source and use Fetch a new CSV in each browser. In the sandbox, use the synthetic source and distinct fictional rows for each fetch. Expect one follow-up per original. Compare Previous batch reference in each draft. Repeating the action from either original reopens its own follow-up.

As First Reviewer, open the submitted follow-ups by Batch reference. Check each batch’s included and excluded rows, then approve or return each independently. The Field Agent transfers each approved batch and follows its own Registry receipt.

As Registry Administrator, compare each follow-up’s receipt with the downloaded audit report. Verify the batch reference, native Registry reference, rows found, rows ingested and attempt count. If another browser has already started a transfer, reload that batch and check its existing receipt. The Second Reviewer sees the Data Imports access guidance for their role.
Review and transfer: Send the reconciled batch for approval. The approver checks included rows and returns issues with a reason when needed. Correct the same batch and send it back for review.
Check the Registry receipt: After approval, the authorised operator uses Transfer to Registry. The Data Bridge sends the included mapped rows to the native import queue. Check the Registry reference and Refresh Registry receipt on the same batch.
If another browser has changed the batch, use Reload batch and check the current status or receipt before transferring again.

Queued status confirms queue acceptance. Ingested by Registry and the receipt counts show native ingestion. If the receipt is partial or needs attention, use row evidence and the native reference for reconciliation. Keep the original batch and audit report. The hosted synthetic source exercises receipt tracking without publishing beneficiary registrations.
Follow up a partial receipt: Refresh the original receipt and compare the ingested and found counts. In Reconcile records, use Issues and exclusions only to find included rows marked No Registry row receipt. Clear the filter to see Registry logged rows. Excluded rows were outside the transfer.

Field Agents send the batch and Registry references and outstanding row numbers to the Registry Administrator. First Reviewers compare the receipt against the approved rows and share any discrepancies. Registry Administrators coordinate native job and row-log reconciliation with the integration owner.

Keep the original receipt and audit report. The Registry worker owns ingestion retries after queue acceptance. After native reconciliation confirms which rows are outstanding, use New import and the approved mapping to upload a separate correction file containing only those rows. Correct the values and keep the existing source keys. Record the original batch reference with the correction evidence.

The First Reviewer checks the correction against the original receipt and the confirmed outstanding rows. The Field Agent transfers the separate batch after approval. Compare the two receipts, then keep both batch and Registry references with the audit reports.
Resolve a repeated correction row: Data Imports blocks an included row when the same source key already has a receipt or is in progress in another batch for the same source and destination mapping. When two approved corrections try to transfer the same row together, the first transfer reserves the row. The other batch stays blocked while that receipt is pending and after the row is received.

If the warning offers Reload batch, use it to update the affected rows. Open the affected row under Reconcile records, then use Open existing batch when available. Refresh the earlier receipt and reopen the blocked batch to see whether the row is still in progress or already received.

Field Agents exclude rows confirmed received from editable drafts. First Reviewers return pending corrections with the earlier batch reference and affected row number. For competing approved batches, Registry Administrators use Activity and the earlier receipt to check which batch entered the queue and preserve both batch references.
Recover when the first correction fails: While the first correction is queued or its outcome is uncertain, the other correction stays blocked. The Registry Administrator checks that the first native job has ended and verifies the outstanding row against the native row logs. Refresh the first receipt so Data Imports can reconcile it.

When the receipt confirms the row stayed outstanding, the Field Agent reopens the already-approved correction. If Transfer to Registry is available, send that batch and check its receipt. The First Reviewer verifies the existing approval and retains the evidence. Keep both Registry references to trace the failed and completed transfers.
Handle a failed job with a received row: A native job can fail after the Registry logs a row. Refresh the original receipt and use Reconcile records to confirm Registry logged. When the receipt shows the row was ingested, the alternate correction stays blocked for that source key.

The Field Agent keeps the receipt and reports the job error. The First Reviewer preserves the approval evidence and both batch references. The Registry Administrator investigates the failure using the existing native Registry reference and row logs.
Handle a saved row with a missing receip: The Registry records the save in the same transaction as the row. If the job fails before writing the normal receipt log, Data Imports shows Registry saved, receipt log missing. Matching alternate corrections stay blocked. A native retry can use the original save when writing the receipt log.

Keep the original Registry reference and audit report. Field Agents report the missing log. First Reviewers preserve approvals and both batch references. Registry Administrators reconcile the save and the missing log with Registry integration support. Older jobs without saved-row tracking need native reconciliation before resubmission.
Verify a restored receipt log: After Registry integration support retries the existing job, use Refresh Registry receipt on the original batch. Confirm Registry logged under Reconcile records and Registry receipt log restored under Activity. Download the audit report to keep the restoration event with the original Registry reference.

Field Agents keep the restored receipt. First Reviewers retain the approval and both batch references. Registry Administrators verify the log against the existing job and saved row. The matching alternate stays blocked.
Check overlapping Registry retries: Two retries of the same native job use the same saved row. When they overlap, Registry workers coordinate writing the receipt so the row ends up with one receipt-log entry. The matching alternate remains blocked while the workers retry and after the receipt is restored.

Use the original Registry reference for reconciliation. The retry count records worker attempts, while Registry logged and Registry receipt log restored show the receipt outcome. The Registry Administrator can confirm the single receipt entry against the saved row with integration support.
Reconcile mixed retry outcomes: If one worker fails while the other is still retrying, the original receipt may temporarily show a failed job and a saved row with a missing log. Keep the matching alternate blocked. When the remaining retry restores the log, refresh the original receipt. The job becomes Processed and clears the earlier job error.
If the worker error arrives after the receipt is restored, the job stays Processed. In either order, verify one saved row and one receipt log under the original Registry reference.

The Field Agent keeps the restored receipt. The First Reviewer preserves the existing approval and both batch references. The Registry Administrator checks the final status and receipt log and keeps the failed attempt with the incident evidence.
Handle two failed receipt retries: If both retries fail before writing the log and the native job has stopped, refresh the original receipt. The job remains Failed and the row stays Registry saved, receipt log missing. The matching alternate remains blocked. Activity and the downloadable audit report preserve the missing-log result.

Field Agents report the condition using the original reference. First Reviewers keep the existing approval and both batch references. Registry Administrators retain the failed attempts and coordinate with integration support to correct the log error and retry the existing job.
Verify recovery after two failed retries: When Registry integration support resolves the log error, a further native retry can restore the missing log on the existing job. Refresh the original receipt and verify Processed, the original Registry reference and one receipt-log entry for the previously saved row. The matching alternate stays blocked.

Keep both failed attempts with the incident evidence. Use the downloadable audit report to retain the Registry receipt log restored event. Field Agents keep the restored receipt, First Reviewers retain the approval and both batch references, and Registry Administrators verify the restored log against the original save.
Verify a retry after receipt restoration: If one or more retry tasks reach the job after the receipt is restored, refresh the original batch in Transfers. The job stays Processed with the same Registry reference, one saved row and one receipt log. Activity and the downloadable audit report retain a single Registry receipt log restored event. The matching alternate stays blocked as Already received by Registry.

The Field Agent keeps the existing receipt and leaves the alternate on hold. The First Reviewer keeps the existing approval and both batch references. The Registry Administrator verifies the existing receipt against the saved row and leaves the completed job closed. If two retries reach the completed job at the same time, ask Registry integration support to verify both deliveries against the original Registry reference.

If one of those retries fails, verify that the original job still shows Processed and the alternate stays blocked. If the first retry fails while the other is still running, refresh the original receipt and verify Processed with one receipt log. Repeat the check after the other retry finishes. Keep the worker error in the integration incident record with the original Registry reference and the existing receipt.
Configure sources and access: Administrators maintain versioned mappings. Check the destination register and template, input connection, required values, field transforms and duplicate key in Sources and mappings. Use Test mapping with sample values before saving an authorised change.
Existing batches retain the mapping version they started with. Access shows the assigned roles for data preparation, independent approval and administration.
Who handles each Data Imports step: The Help panel calls the Registry Field Agent the Operator and the Registry First Reviewer the Approver. A Second Reviewer uses the Registry Level 2 task queue and sees access guidance in Data Imports. Registry Administrator is the configuration role.

The Operator prepares the batch and sends it for independent approval. The Approver reviews the batch. After approval, an authorised operator transfers it, then checks the original Registry receipt. Use the exception sections below if the transfer returns a partial receipt.

pages.title: Offline field collection and ODK
pages.description: Capture field interviews on an authorised device and follow the import into the Registry.

Set up field capture: Open Offline field capture through the assigned Registry account. Use the approved ODK Collect configuration and install the assigned form before travelling offline. Keep configuration codes within the authorised team.
Capture and send: Complete the household interview and save it on the device. When connected again, check which forms were sent successfully. ODK Central supports staff oversight of forms and submissions.
Verify the handoff: Check the matching Registry intake reference. The configured native import writes intake records for review. The current approver determines progression to the master register.

pages.title: Social Registry administration
pages.description: Find older registry records and manage the reference lists used by that workspace.

Find legacy records: Use the earlier Social Registry workspace for its existing registrant and group records. Use the Master Registry for new native intake and its Level 1 and Level 2 workflow.
Maintain authorised reference data: Review relationships, ID types, tags and district settings where available to your administrative role. Confirm downstream use before changing shared options.

pages.title: Beneficiary Portal
pages.description: Find available programmes and track the status of an application.

Find registers and programmes: Use Registries to find an applicable registration path. Use Programmes to check which programme applications are available and what information they require.
Apply and track: Complete the application for the selected programme. Keep the application reference and check your status in the corresponding workspace.
Check the right record: A beneficiary application, a registration and a payment each have their own status. Use the reference tied to the item you are following.

pages.title: PBMS programme setup
pages.description: Set up the programme, registry, eligibility, benefits and staff assignments.

Prepare approved configuration: Select the target registry and the applicable benefit code, unit and quantity. Confirm the eligibility expression against the approved criteria, including any PMT rule, cutoff and version. Check which fields are supported on the selected registry.
Set up the programme: Use Programmes or the programme approval flow. Assign programme staff, including separate Payment, Finance, Audit and CEO roles where configured. Programme Admin maintains programme setup and sponsor routing.
Check connected resources: Review programme benefits, agencies, warehouses or sponsor-bank routes where required by the delivery model. Verify units, beneficiary populations and cycle dates before creating lists.

pages.title: Cycles and beneficiary lists
pages.description: Set enrolment and disbursement windows, calculate lists and verify the included beneficiaries.

Set the cycle dates: Check the approved programme calendar. Use the enrolment cycle’s registration and disbursement windows and the linked disbursement cycle schedule date.
Calculate and verify the lists: Open the cycle and calculate its list using the configured criteria. Compare the beneficiary count, included and excluded lines, benefits and totals to the approved scope. Check that the correct cycle and revision are selected.
Trace eligibility and entitlements: Inspect the enrolment or disbursement workflow for the current results and checks. Use the applicable programme and registry reference when following an exclusion or entitlement.

pages.title: PBMS approvals and corrections
pages.description: Initiate approval, record Finance, Audit and CEO decisions, and resubmit corrected lists.

Initiate approval: Payment opens the completed list and starts approval for the current revision. Finance, Audit and CEO then make their own decisions when the corresponding stage opens.
Follow each approval stage: Finance checks the programme, cycle, approved scope and amounts against the current list. Audit checks the approval history, supporting evidence and traceability for that revision. The CEO reviews the completed earlier decisions and makes the final decision. Each role acts from its assigned stage and records its decision in the approval history.
Return and correct: The current approver records a reason when returning a list. Programme Admin opens the affected beneficiaries, makes the approved correction and saves the correction reason. Payment checks the saved correction and resubmits the list.
Check the revision and outcome: Corrected resubmission starts a new revision at Finance. Reviewing staff confirm they are deciding the current revision. After final approval, check routing and payment readiness in the Payments section.

pages.title: Payments and reconciliation
pages.description: Submit the approved list, read Bridge reports and handle partial outcomes.

Route and submit: Programme Admin saves the approved sponsor bank route for the verified list. Payment opens Proceed to payments and confirms the revision, beneficiary count, total and route. Keep the submitted envelope and batch references.
Read the reports: Open View payment progress and select the applicable report. The batch report shows financial-address resolution and sponsor bank dispatch. The envelope report shows declared, received, shipped, reconciled and reversed instruction counts. Refresh the report when Bridge is still preparing it.
Handle a partial outcome: Payment retains the original references and sends affected instruction IDs to Finance. Finance checks the available statement entries and separates outstanding and reversed instructions. Audit checks traceability. Programme Admin coordinates the authorised follow-up, and the CEO handles escalated decisions where required.
Confirm settlement evidence: Use the underlying statement evidence and amounts for financial conclusions. Disbursement counters describe instruction status, and bank dispatch completion describes the dispatch step.
Follow one instruction through reconcili: Payment follows the approved list revision, batch, envelope and instruction. On a submitted sandbox list, open the Finance case queue to hand an unresolved instruction to Finance. Finance acknowledges the same case and uses the linked instruction and statement evidence.

Finance records the instruction-level outcome and an independent Finance reviewer checks it. Retain the original case and add later evidence to its history. Use the existing case reference when escalating an amount difference. The five operational Finance procedures await Finance sign-off.

pages.title: Reversals and reconciliation exceptions
pages.description: Work with bank reversals, repeated statement entries and differences in reported amounts.

Verify a reversal: Confirm the instruction, original payment, statement entry and amount. Record the reversal against the existing case or reconciliation record. Keep any original approved invoice or list evidence traceable.
Check repeated statement entries: Bridge counts a repeated reversal for the same instruction once. If another statement shows a different amount, Bridge reports a reconciliation exception. Finance compares both statement entries before changing the case outcome. Audit retains the decision trail.
Follow corrective and reopened cases: Track each authorised corrective payment on its separately approved list, with its own envelope and batch. If a corrective payment reverses, keep both histories together for escalated review. Use the authorised decision record when escalating, closing or reopening a case after a later reversal.
Make a decision on a closed or reopened: If a later statement confirms a new reversal on a payment already issued under a closed case, Finance and Audit verify the bank evidence before the case is considered for reopening. Keep the closure, reopening and supporting evidence under the same case reference. If the CEO authorises a further payment, follow a separate approved list through payment and reconciliation. If the CEO closes the reopened case, retain the decision and payment history.

If the later statement repeats a reversal already recorded at the same amount, retain it as duplicate evidence and keep the case closed. If the amount differs, check the Bridge reversal amount exception and keep the original reversal and later statement linked for Finance and Audit review before the CEO makes any new case decision.
Record the next action: Payment tracks the affected instructions with Finance. Programme Admin coordinates the approved follow-up. Audit reviews evidence and the CEO records any escalated decision under the approved procedure.

pages.title: Bridge and account mapping
pages.description: Understand how PBMS instructions reach the sponsor bank and return as reconciliation evidence.

Payment handoff: PBMS submits approved instructions to Bridge through the configured integration. An envelope groups the disbursement instructions and a batch tracks the related dispatch.
Resolve financial addresses: Bridge uses the configured account mapper, including SPAR where enabled, to resolve a beneficiary reference to a financial address. Review resolution and dispatch status through the batch report and authorised integration support.
Read statement outcomes: In the sandbox, the configured Example Bank route can exercise synthetic dispatch and statement processing. Finance uses statement references and the envelope report to confirm outcomes and investigate reversals.

pages.title: Beneficiary programme administration
pages.description: Maintain programme and application settings for the separate beneficiary workspace.

Configure applicant-facing programmes: Use this workspace to maintain beneficiary programme visibility, application forms and related records available to assigned administrators. Check the resulting applicant experience in the Beneficiary Portal.
Identify the delivery workspace: The beneficiary application administrator and PBMS 3 use separate programme models in this installation. Confirm the applicable integration before following an application into a PBMS programme or disbursement list.

pages.title: Staff access and identity
pages.description: Find assigned services and administer authorised roles and access.

Open assigned services: Sign in to the Staff Portal with the assigned staff account. Use the service tiles for your work. Some applications require a separate programme or record-scope assignment.
Request or maintain access: Use the approved identity administration process for staff roles and service access. Registry scope, PBMS programme membership and independent review duties are controlled in the relevant service.
Investigate missing access: Provide the service name, account email, expected role and record or programme reference to authorised support. Keep passwords, tokens and full beneficiary identifiers out of support messages.

pages.title: Approval Workflow Engine
pages.description: Follow assigned decisions, request history and configured approval policies.

Follow the request: Open the request associated with the intake or change. Check its current stage, assignment and decision history. Use the originating workspace when the task is managed there.
Review callback and history: Check recent decisions and whether the originating service reflects the resulting status. Provide the request and artifact references to support when recorded states disagree.
Maintain policies and assignments: Authorised administrators use the controls enabled for their role to inspect workflow policies, versions and delegation. Confirm the approved workflow and test it with synthetic cases before relying on new rules.

pages.title: Master data and geography
pages.description: Use shared reference lists and maintain the state, LGA and ward hierarchy.

Check the hierarchy: Select the correct State or FCT before inspecting the available LGA and ward values. Use the reference code and parent area when checking an import mapping.
Maintain reference values: Assigned administrators check the intended code, validity and downstream mappings before proposing changes. Report unavailable areas with their parent reference and the source used to verify them.
Interpret reported coordinates: Captured GPS data describes the reading and its reported accuracy. Use the approved procedure to validate location, handle missing values and resolve boundary questions.

pages.title: Partner management
pages.description: Review partner records, onboarding requests and authorised integration scope.

Find or review a partner: Open the directory and confirm the organisation and reference. Use the relevant request and approval history for onboarding or changes.
Review integration access: Check the approved partner scope and current connection details with authorised administrators. Coordinate changes using the managed workflow and keep credentials in designated secret-handling channels.

pages.title: Consent management
pages.description: Follow partner consent approvals and recorded decisions.

Identify the decision and scope: Confirm the partner, request and relevant data scope before reviewing approvals or recorded decisions. Use the corresponding view available to your role.
Resolve consent questions: Check the applicable consent record, approved sharing rules and any recorded follow-up. Send unresolved questions to the authorised consent owner with the request reference.

pages.title: Analytics and geographic records
pages.description: Check workflow totals, programme reporting and geographic coverage.

Choose the reporting workspace: Use platform Analytics for connected service summaries, the PBMS analytics view for programme measures and Superset for authorised dashboards. Check the scope, time period and refresh status before comparing counts.
Read geographic coverage: Use Geographic record data to inspect coverage, grouped counts and reported coordinates. Check what location fields are available before interpreting gaps.
Export within your permissions: Use the authorised export where available. Keep the applied filters and reporting date with the extract so other staff can reproduce the figures.

pages.title: Phase 1 sandbox workspaces
pages.description: Explore the programme demo, grievance handling, field capture and conditionality.

Explore the programme demo: Open the Phase 1 sandbox to inspect the connected demonstration stages and synthetic case evidence. The readiness view shows the available checks for assigned staff.
Track grievances and attendance: Use the relevant Phase 1 workspace for grievance cases or conditionality. Inspect the case, recorded activity and verification status with the assigned role.
Use field and publication tools: The Phase 1 field workspace supports synthetic capture workflows. Authorised content staff use the CMS for public programme information and its review and publication history.

pages.title: Help and troubleshooting
pages.description: Choose the right guidance and collect the details needed to resolve an issue.

Open contextual Help: Select Help on the current screen or use a field’s Help icon. The available guidance follows the service, screen, role and workflow state. The Knowledge Library also supports browsing by task and service.
Find task and role guidance in the docs: Open a service guide from the Service directory. Task and field reference includes contextual Help for workflows, screens and individual fields. Knowledge Library articles include additional tasks and guidance for specific audiences. Use Search to find either by task or role.

Open in Knowledge Library takes you to the published source article. Upstream references describe OpenG2P features and release-dependent behaviour. Confirm availability in NSIPA before using them for an operational decision.
Make the issue reproducible: Record the workspace, timestamp, action, status and relevant non-sensitive references. Note whether the action succeeded before retrying a submission or transfer. Share the evidence with your service administrator.
Report a guidance gap: Share the guide title or ID, version, workspace, screen and expected next action with your service administrator. Include non-sensitive evidence so the content team can check the applicable version.

pages.title: Jos Family Support demo
pages.description: Explore the conditional cash transfer journey using a fictional programme.

Follow the demonstration: Open Jos Family Support to see how a conditional cash transfer programme connects household intake, programme decisions and payment reporting.
Use the demo’s sample cases to understand the journey and the responsibilities at each stage. Use the corresponding staff workspace for your assigned synthetic records.
Read the operational guides: Use the programme setup, conditionality and reconciliation guides when you need the workflow details behind a demo stage.

pages.title: Field interaction preview
pages.description: Walk through the field app screens before setting up connected capture.

Explore the interface: Use the interaction preview to understand the form sequence and saved-visit workflow with sample data.
Move to field capture: For an assigned connected exercise, use the approved capture and synchronisation method. Confirm the submission in the Registry before reviewer action.

pages.title: Nigeria Territorial Intelligence atlas
pages.description: Explore the public territorial maps and their source notes.

Browse reference geography: Select the area in the public atlas and examine its displayed geographic and territorial data. Read the source and reference dates for the view you are comparing.
Choose the right map: Use the atlas for public territorial reference. Use Geographic record data in the staff workspace to inspect the location coverage of synthetic registration records.
